headline: Macron Outlines Conditional Gathering Bans and Crisis Cell After French Unrest
deck: France’s president set out security, aid and consultation measures after unrest in French cities; the Interior Ministry reported about 2,400 arrests and 1,000 police officers injured on Saturday.
body: French President Emmanuel Macron addressed the country after unrest in cities across France, calling the moment one of “extreme gravity.” [E1]
Macron said prefects, working with mayors, could ban certain gatherings when necessary to protect cities, public buildings and shops. [E2]
He said the prime minister would chair a crisis cell on 19 October to mobilize rapid aid for people affected by the unrest. [E3]
Macron also said students, teachers, unions, employers, local authorities and lawmakers would work with the government that week on concrete proposals. [E4]
France’s Interior Ministry reported about 2,400 arrests during the unrest, BBC News reported. [E5]
The ministry also reported about 1,000 police officers injured on Saturday, including seven seriously injured, BBC News reported. [E6]
